messages:
pagerbot: [ALERT] rtx-prefix-cache: sudden drop in prefix hit-rate on prod us-west-2 (p99 latency ↑, error spike). page=1 severity=high. Paging ops-oncall @Anna K and infra-oncall @Jordan P :rotating_light:
Anna K: on it. seeing increased 5xxs from conv-service behind gateway. metrics: prefix_hit_rate from 94% -> 61% in last 6m.
Jordan P: can you paste the query or dashboard link?
Anna K: dashboard: https://dash.redwood.internal/d/rtx/cache-prefix?from=now-15m
Anna K: quick grep shows 504s correlate with cache-miss paths hitting fallback model pool.
Sandeep R: I see the same. logs show rewarm jobs failing with zlib decode errors around 2019994250 onwards.
Leila T: customer impact? any heavy tenants affected?
Maria G: CB-analytics saw latency spikes, reported errors in their ingestion pipeline. CS pinged us on call.
Tim O: rolling mitigation - we can flip prefix-eviction-policy to conservative and enable auto-rewarm for hot prefixes. plan to throttle eviction to 20% for 10m.
Anna K: executing: `infractl cache update --pool-prefix rtx --eviction-rate 0.2 --duration 10m`
Jordan P: heads up, that will increase memory - we have headroom on node group a.
Anna K: done. response: OK.
pagerbot: Deploy started by Anna K: infractl v2.1.4.
Sandeep R: while we mitigate, can folks add timeline and paste logs here. I'll start a hypothesis list.
Anna K: timeline so far: 2019994200 - small bump in evictions; 2019994250 - rewarm job errors (zlib decode); 2019994321 - pager alert when hit-rate dropped; 2019994400 - fallback model traffic increase 3x; 2019994600 - mitigation eviction-rate lowered; 2019994800 - partial recovery but hit-rate still ~78%.
Jordan P: logs (sampling): ```
[2026-03-12T21:04:10Z] rewarm-worker-3 ERROR zlib: unexpected EOF
[2026-03-12T21:04:11Z] cache-node-7 WARN eviction: cascade trigger idx=12
[2026-03-12T21:04:12Z] prefix-router INFO miss route=fallback model=redwood-v1
```
Sandeep R: hypothesis A: rewarm blob corruption -> failed to populate local KV -> high cold misses.
Sandeep R: hypothesis B: TTL mis-sync after recent index-roll (last night) caused mass invalidation across prefixes.
Leila T: hypothesis C: KV reuse logic race — nodes claiming warmed prefixes but not actually serving KV due to inconsistent manifest. That would look like hit-rate drop + logs showing serve attempts with missing keys.
Maria G: adding customer telemetry: CB-analytics shows a 20% request fail rate for requests with long context. suspect prefixes for long-context sessions.
Tim O: quick check: `kubectl get pods -n cache | grep rewarm` shows rewarm workers restarting 3x in last 30m. Could be memory fragmentation or corrupted payloads.
Anna K: I uploaded rewarm blob sample to /var/tmp/rewarm-sample-2019994321.gz and checksum mismatch compared to S3 obj: `s3://cache-warmups/prefixes/2026-03-12/20199942.gz` -> local sha256 != s3 sha256.
Jordan P: that supports hypothesis A. Any recent change to rewarm pipeline? deploy 2026-03-11 touched compression flags.
Sandeep R: rolling back compression-change is an option. But we should avoid full rollback if narrow fix possible. Can we re-trigger rewarm using safe decode path (no streaming) to bypass zlib bug?
Anna K: I'll trigger a targeted rewarm for top-50 hot prefixes with safe decode: `rehydrate --prefix-list hot50 --decode-mode=safe`
Anna K: started rehydrate job id=reh-2019994470
Tim O: also increased cache ttl on hot prefixes by +30s to reduce thrash while rewarm finishes.
Maria G: CS updated customer-facing status page: "We are investigating increased latency for embeddings and chat. A subset of customers may see elevated errors."
Leila T: adding to timeline: 2019994470 rehydrate kicked, 2019994520 rewarm worker logs show successful decode for sample blobs.
Sandeep R: new logs (sample): ```
[2026-03-12T21:08:45Z] rehydrate-req INFO prefix=abc123 decode=ok size=1.2MB
[2026-03-12T21:08:46Z] cache-node-4 INFO put prefix=abc123 kv_count=42
[2026-03-12T21:08:48Z] router INFO prefix_hit_rate p99=0.82
```
Anna K: hit-rate trending up to 82% but some suffixes still low. need to validate whether some prefix batches were skipped.
Jordan P: checking manifest sync: `manifestctl diff --since=2026-03-11` shows 3 nodes with stale manifest versions (node-7, node-9, node-12). Those correlate with nodes that had rewarm failures.
Sandeep R: that suggests a race: nodes restarted, got stale manifest, attempted to rewarm with older compression flags causing decode failures.
Leila T: mitigation: I will drain node-7 and force manifest refresh.
Leila T: `nodectl drain node-7 && manifestctl refresh --node node-7`
Leila T: done. node-7 manifest now matches head.
Tim O: we should build a replay to test rewarm decode edge cases in CI. I'll file a follow-up.
Anna K: current customer impact: mitigated to degraded for most tenants. CB-analytics still seeing some errors for long-context flows.
Maria G: CS updated customers: we told CB-analytics they'll see reduced errors in next 30m.
Sandeep R: owners and action items: owner=Sandeep R; follow-ups: (1) root cause doc (rewarm compression mismatch + manifest race) (2) add manifest version checks before rewarm jobs (3) add sha256 checksum verification in rewarm pipeline (4) e2e CI for rewarm with older manifests (5) automate TTL bump on major rewarm ops.
Anna K: who can take (2) and (3)? Jordan?
Jordan P: I'll take (2) manifest pre-check. Tim take (3) checksum and CI tests?
Tim O: yup I'll do (3) and (4).
Leila T: I'm capturing timeline and raw logs into incident RCA doc: https://docs.redwood.internal/incidents/2019994321-rca
Anna K: handing off to night oncall @Sandeep R — please continue collection and start RCA. I'm going offline in 20m.
Sandeep R: acknowledged, taking over. will post interim RCA summary by +6h.
pagerbot: Incident status changed to: mitigated -> degraded. Priority: P2.
Maria G: final note: we should proactively notify customers on dedicated plans about rewarm inconsistencies; also check Dedicated capacity reserved pools for similar manifest drift.
Anna K: thanks all. closing live triage channel in 10m.
